summary: Remote WebSocket server controls shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade on the installer's host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a persistent client that connects to a WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL,.claude-agent.json, or ~/.config/yeaft-agent/config.json) and dispatches server-sent frames to privileged sinks on the installer's machine. A `terminal_create` frame spawns the user's login shell (or PowerShell) inside a PTY via node-pty, and subsequent `terminal_input` frames feed remote bytes directly into `ptyProcess.write(msg.data)`, producing full interactive command execution as the service account. Additional handlers perform arbitrary filesystem writes and an `upgrade_agent` frame invokes `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest`, writes a bash script into the user's config directory, executes it detached, and restarts the process via `systemctl --user` or `launchctl`. service/linux.js also mutates PATH (`~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`) as part of service setup. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket endpoint has interactive shell access and a remote-triggered code-update channel on every host running the agent; the localhost default is only protective while no attacker has local or same-LAN reach or the ability to influence the config file.
